based_on.change: Sell a fixed monthly creative package ($1,200 for 8 ad-ready videos with hooks), not a 20% commission, to Shopify brands spending $5-30K/month on Meta ads

product.name: Hookline Studio
product.one_liner: 8 ad-ready UGC videos a month, with the hooks written for you, for a fixed $1,200. Start with a $799 pilot of 4 videos.
product.customer: US Shopify brands spending $5-30K a month on Meta or TikTok ads, with no in-house creative team
product.problem: Ad creative fatigue raises their CPA, so they need 3-5 fresh product videos a month, and self-serve platforms leave the brief, the hooks and the creator management to the founder

key_metric.name: Paid $799 pilots
key_metric.target: 1 or more paid pilot by day 14

stack.choice: Static one-page offer + Stripe Payment Links + Instantly cold email + a Python stdlib ops tracker (CSV)
stack.why: This is a service, not software: the only things to build are an offer page, a way to get paid and a way to measure hours per video against the kill criteria. Static HTML hosts for free, Stripe has no monthly fee, the tracker needs no install, and the whole thing fits the verdict's $86/month tool budget and 15 hours a week.

components.name: Payments
components.tool: Stripe Payment Links (2.9% + 30c per charge, no monthly fee)

components.name: Offer page hosting
components.tool: Static HTML on any free static host

alternatives.name: Self-serve UGC platform as the back office (Insense, JoinBrands)
alternatives.why_not: Insense starts near $400/month and JoinBrands charges 8-15% per order: that eats the margin, and the brand can see the same platform and go direct.

alternatives.name: No-code client portal (Airtable or Notion with forms)
alternatives.why_not: Useful at 5+ clients, but a portal for 1-2 pilot clients is time the verdict says goes to sales; a CSV tracker answers the only question that matters now: hours per video.

env.name: TRACKER_DATA_DIR
env.purpose: Folder where ops/tracker.py keeps its CSV files (default ops/data, which is gitignored)

env.name: HOURLY_FLOOR_USD
env.purpose: Effective hourly rate under which the tracker flags the kill criterion (default 20)

structure.purpose: The one-page offer: $799 pilot and $1,200/month package
Offer page with the two Stripe Payment Link buttons (paste the links in)
Brand colours and type from design-tokens.css
Cold email and LinkedIn message templates with the personalisation slots
Brief per video: product, angle, 3 hooks, shot list, deadline
Fixed-rate creator agreement: usage rights scope, FTC disclosure, payment terms
Pilot and monthly package terms: deliverables, revisions, notice, no direct hire of creators
Logs outreach, orders, videos and hours; reports the kill criteria
CSV data written by the tracker (never committed)
Keeps client and creator data out of git
Tests for the tracker's math and kill-criteria flags

personas.name: Maya, DTC founder
personas.role: Founder of a US Shopify brand spending $5-30K a month on Meta ads, no creative team
personas.pain: Her ads fatigue every 4-8 weeks; she needs 3-5 new videos a month and has no time to brief and chase creators

personas.name: Jordan, UGC creator
personas.role: US creator filming product videos at a fixed $100-150 per video
personas.pain: UGC rates fell 44% in 2025 and work is irregular; wants steady, clearly briefed orders paid on time

personas.role: The founder running the studio solo, 15 hours a week, $1,000 budget
personas.pain: Every hour of coordination lowers the hourly rate; needs to know fast whether the model pays

stories.want: a one-page offer that states the $799 pilot (4 videos with hooks) and the $1,200/month package, with a pay button
stories.so_that: I can decide and pay without a call
acceptance: The page shows both prices, the number of videos, revisions (2) and turnaround (10 days)
The pilot button opens a Stripe Payment Link for $799 and a test payment succeeds

stories.want: a list of 100 Shopify brands in one vertical running Meta ads, each with a founder email
stories.so_that: the 7-day test has a real audience
acceptance: 100 rows with brand, Meta Ad Library link and founder email
Every brand has an ad active in the last 30 days

stories.want: a fixed-rate agreement that states pay, usage rights and disclosure rules
stories.so_that: I know what I am paid and how my video will be used
acceptance: 3 creators accept a fixed rate between $100 and $150 per video in writing
The agreement states licence scope and duration and an FTC disclosure clause

stories.want: to send 100 personalised cold emails and 30 LinkedIn messages and log every reply
stories.so_that: I can apply the day-7 kill rule on real numbers
acceptance: tracker.py shows 100 emails and 30 LinkedIn messages sent
tracker.py report prints positive replies and flags fewer than 3 as STOP

stories.want: a short creative brief per video with 3 hooks to approve before anything is filmed
stories.so_that: the videos test angles I believe in
acceptance: 4 briefs filled from the template, each with product, angle, 3 hooks and a shot list
Maya approves the briefs in writing before the product ships to creators

stories.want: to log hours per order and see hours per video and my effective hourly rate
stories.so_that: I know if I hit the 2-hours-per-video kill criterion
acceptance: tracker.py report prints hours per video and USD per hour for each order
An order above 2 hours per video or under HOURLY_FLOOR_USD is flagged STOP
Unit tests cover both flags

stories.want: 4 ad-ready vertical videos with captions within 10 days of the creators receiving the product
stories.so_that: I can launch them in Ads Manager right away
acceptance: 4 files at 1080x1920 with captions and the hook in the first 3 seconds
Delivered within 10 days of product receipt, with up to 2 revisions done

stories.want: a proposal to continue at $1,200/month for 8 videos, sent right after the pilot
stories.so_that: I keep a steady flow of new ads without re-briefing a new vendor
acceptance: Proposal sent within 3 days of pilot delivery
A $1,200/month Stripe subscription link works in test mode

stories.want: a monthly recap of which hooks won, from the numbers I share from Ads Manager
stories.so_that: next month's videos build on what worked
acceptance: The recap lists spend, CTR and CPA per video from client-shared numbers
It names the 8 hooks for next month

stories.want: a client agreement with a 30-day notice and a no-direct-hire clause for 12 months
stories.so_that: a client cannot take my creators after the first order
acceptance: The agreement states deliverables, revisions, 30-day notice and the no-direct-hire term
Every paying client has signed it before production starts

stories.want: a monthly production calendar for 2 package clients (16 videos)
stories.so_that: production stays inside 15 hours a week
acceptance: 16 videos scheduled with brief, ship, film and delivery dates
tracker.py shows 2 hours or less per video for the month

stories.want: to be paid within 7 days of the brand approving my video
stories.so_that: I keep taking the studio's orders
acceptance: tracker.py records approval and payment dates per video
Every creator payment of the month is 7 days or less after approval

stories.want: a short case study from the pilot results on the offer page
stories.so_that: I can trust the studio before paying
acceptance: The case study uses numbers the client approved in writing
The page shows it with the client's permission

sprints.name: The 7-day test
sprints.goal: Run the verdict's 7-day test: 100 brands listed, 3 creators signed, offer page and payment link live, 100 cold emails sent, every positive reply asked for a paid pilot
sprints.exit: 3 or more positive replies from 100 emails by day 7 and 1 or more paid $799 deposit by day 14; otherwise stop

sprints.name: Deliver the pilot
sprints.goal: Brief, film and deliver the first 4 videos while logging every hour
sprints.exit: 4 videos delivered within 10 days of product receipt, at 2 hours or less per video (8 hours total)

sprints.name: Convert to the package
sprints.goal: Turn the pilot into the $1,200/month package with a results recap and a signed agreement
sprints.exit: 1 client signed on the $1,200/month package and paid the first month

sprints.name: Repeatable month
sprints.goal: Run a full month for 2 package clients inside 15 hours a week
sprints.exit: 2 active package clients, 16 videos scheduled, 2 hours or less per video and creators paid within 7 days

dod: In app/, python3 -m unittest discover -s tests passes
Every acceptance criterion was checked on the real thing (real brand, real email, real payment link, real video), not a mock
The README Run commands still work from a clean clone
No secrets, client data or creator personal data in git (.env and ops/data are ignored)
The hours spent on the story are logged in ops/tracker.py
The customer (brand or creator) saw the result and answered

revenue_per_customer_month.reasoning: The rescue path's fixed package: $1,200 a month for 8 ad-ready videos (verdict rescue 1)

variable_cost_per_customer_month.reasoning: 8 videos x $100 creator fixed rate (low end of the verdict's $100-150) = $800, plus card fee 2.9% x $1,200 + $0.30 = $35.10; product shipping paid by the brand; founder hours excluded

cac.reasoning: ($86 tools + 15 h outreach x $20/h) / about 1.3 clients per 100 emails; a $1,200 retainer closes less often than the verdict's $190 commission CAC

churn_monthly_pct.reasoning: Retainers lose 1.6% a month per the verdict's benchmark, but small brands and a new solo studio churn more: assumed 12-month lifetime

fixed_costs_month.reasoning: Instantly $47 + lead finder $9 + ~$30 domains and inboxes

start_cash.reasoning: The founder's stated budget in idea.context: USD 1,000
